note: classic order: welcome and announcements, sermon, benediction
text: [[announcements]] Good morning, church! It's so good to see you. If you're a first time guest, we're glad you're here, please fill out a connection card and drop it in the offering plate. A couple of things this week. Wednesday night supper starts back at 5:30 in the fellowship hall, and the youth will be serving. The ladies are collecting coats for the shelter through the end of the month, there's a bin in the foyer. And don't forget the work day Saturday morning at 8. [[/]] Alright, open your Bibles to Mark chapter 4. Mark 4, starting in verse 35. That day when evening came, he said to his disciples, let us go over to the other side. Now I want you to notice something about this storm. Jesus is the one who told them to get in the boat. They did not wander into trouble by disobeying. They were exactly where he sent them, and the storm came anyway. Some of you are in a storm this week and you have been asking what you did wrong. Maybe nothing. Obedience does not buy you calm water. The disciples woke him and said, Teacher, don't you care if we drown? That is an honest prayer. It is not a polite prayer, but it is honest. And notice he does not scold them for waking him. He rebukes the wind first and then he asks them about their faith. The order matters. He deals with the storm and then he deals with the heart. Who is this, they ask, that even the wind and the waves obey him? That is the question the whole gospel of Mark is asking. Who is this? And the answer is that the one asleep in the stern is the Lord of the sea. The Lord bless you and keep you, the Lord make his face shine upon you and be gracious to you. [[announcements]] Hey, before you go, the Henderlys are hosting lunch for newcomers today, just meet them by the welcome center. Have a great week. [[/]]

note: prayer requests in the middle, pastoral prayer with names
text: Good morning. We are in week three of our series in Philippians. If you have your Bible turn with me to Philippians chapter 2. Have this mind among yourselves, which is yours in Christ Jesus, who, though he was in the form of God, did not count equality with God a thing to be grasped. Paul is not writing a theology lecture here. He is writing to a church that is fighting. Euodia and Syntyche could not get along, and Paul's answer to a church fight is a hymn about the incarnation. That tells you something. The cure for pride is not a rule. It is a picture of Christ. He emptied himself. He took the form of a servant. [[prayer]] Before we go further I want to stop and pray for our church family. We have some needs this morning. Please be praying for Delphine Ostrow, she had her surgery on Thursday and she is recovering at home. Pray for the Kettering family as they grieve the loss of their father, the funeral will be Tuesday. And Brother Amos asked us to keep his grandson in your prayers, he deploys next week. Let's pray. Father, we lift up Delphine and ask for healing. We pray comfort over the Kettering family. Protect young Caleb as he goes. Amen. [[/]] So Paul says, do nothing from selfish ambition or conceit, but in humility count others more significant than yourselves. Notice he does not say think less of yourself. He says count others more significant. Humility is not low self esteem. It is a different direction of attention. The proud person is always looking in the mirror. The humble person is looking out the window. And the reason we can do that is that Christ did it first. Therefore God has highly exalted him. The way up is down. That is the shape of the gospel and it is the shape of the Christian life.

note: testimony before the sermon, no announcements
text: [[testimony]] This morning Rosalind Mbeki is going to share with us what God has been doing in her life. Rosalind, come on up. Thank you, Pastor. Three years ago I would not have been in this room. I was drinking every day and I had lost my job and my kids would not talk to me. My sister kept inviting me to this church and I kept saying no. One Sunday I came just to get her to stop asking. I sat in the back row and I left before the last song. But something in what was said stayed with me. I came back the next week. I met with Pastor and he did not lecture me. He just listened. I have been sober for two years now. My daughter comes with me now. I'm not saying everything is fixed, but God did not give up on me. Thank you for sharing that, Rosalind. Let's thank God for what he has done. [[/]] Well, that is a hard act to follow, and it fits our passage this morning. Turn with me to Luke 15. A man had two sons. You know the story. The younger son asks for his inheritance, which is a way of saying I wish you were dead. He goes to a far country and wastes it all. And when he comes to himself, he goes home rehearsing a speech. But the father sees him while he is still a long way off. He runs. In that culture an old man did not run. He lifts his robes and runs and he falls on his son's neck before the speech is even finished. The son never gets to the part where he says make me a hired servant. Grace interrupts the speech. And then there is the older brother, who never left home and never understood his father either. Jesus leaves that story open on purpose.

note: hard negatives: sermon about prayer and Sunday, no gold stretches
text: Turn with me to Matthew 6. And when you pray, you must not be like the hypocrites. For they love to stand and pray in the synagogues and at the street corners. Jesus is not against public prayer. He is against prayer as a performance. The question is who your audience is. Some of you pray every day and some of you have not prayed in years. Here is what I want you to do this week. Find a closet. Literally, if you have to. Shut the door. Say something honest to your Father who sees in secret. You do not need many words. The pagans think they will be heard for their many words. Your Father knows what you need before you ask him. So why pray at all? Because prayer is not information. It is relationship. A child does not tell a father she is hungry because the father does not know. She tells him because he is her father. Pray then like this. Our Father in heaven, hallowed be your name. Notice that the first request is not about you. It is about his name. On the first day of the week the women went to the tomb and found it empty, and every Sunday since has been a little Easter. That is why we gather on this day. Not because Sunday is magic but because the resurrection changed the calendar of the church. The testimony of the apostles is that he is alive. That is what we stand on.

note: pastor's own hospital story is sermon content, then a short prayer request
text: I spent a lot of time in the hospital last year with my father. Some of you know that. He was there for six weeks and I learned more about waiting than I ever wanted to. You sit in those plastic chairs and you watch the monitors and you realize you are not in control of anything. That is where Psalm 13 found me. How long, O Lord? Will you forget me forever? David is not afraid to ask God how long. And then at the end of the psalm, with nothing changed outwardly, he says, but I have trusted in your steadfast love. The circumstances did not change. The direction of his trust did. Waiting is not wasted time when you are waiting on God. [[prayer]] On that note, our prayer chain asked me to mention Wendell Ashgrove, who goes in for chemo again on Monday. Please keep him and his wife Corinne in your prayers this week. [[/]] Let me say one more thing about lament. Lament is a form of faith. You only complain to someone you believe can do something about it. Atheists do not lament. They just despair. When you bring your how long to God you are confessing that he is able.

note: baptism testimony read by the candidate, then the sermon
text: [[testimony]] Today we are celebrating a baptism. Before we go down to the water, Tobias wants to share his story. Hi everybody. I grew up in church but I never really believed it for myself. Last spring my best friend died in a car accident and I was really angry at God. I stopped coming. My youth leader, Ms. Harlow, kept texting me every week even when I never answered. In the summer I went to camp and one night I just broke down and told God I was done running. I want to be baptized because I want everyone to know I belong to Jesus now. Give him a hand, church! [[/]] Our text this morning is Romans 6. What shall we say then? Are we to continue in sin that grace may abound? By no means! How can we who died to sin still live in it? Do you not know that all of us who have been baptized into Christ Jesus were baptized into his death? Baptism is a funeral and a birthday at the same time. The old you goes into the water and a new you comes out. That is not because the water is magic. It is because of the union with Christ that the water pictures. We were buried with him by baptism into death, in order that, just as Christ was raised from the dead by the glory of the Father, we too might walk in newness of life.

note: announcements without the word, spread over the welcome
text: [[announcements]] Welcome, welcome. Grab a seat, there's room up front. So the student ministry is heading to the beach retreat in two weeks and they still need drivers, so if you have a minivan and a free weekend, find Deshawn. Also the nursery has moved to the new wing, just follow the signs. And thank you to everyone who brought food for the Okafor family last week, they were so blessed. [[/]] Let's read together from Isaiah 40. Comfort, comfort my people, says your God. Speak tenderly to Jerusalem, and cry to her that her warfare is ended. Isaiah is speaking to people in exile. They have lost everything. The temple is gone. The city is gone. And the first word God sends them is comfort. Not a lecture. Not a list of what they did wrong, although they did plenty wrong. Comfort. A voice cries, in the wilderness prepare the way of the Lord. God is coming to them. They cannot get home, so he will come to them. That is the gospel in the Old Testament. All flesh is grass, the grass withers, the flower fades, but the word of our God will stand forever.
